change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Queries are interpolated here and again by DataSourceWithBackend.query, so ad hoc filters get added more than once
findings.body:
`applyTemplateVariables` appends ad hoc filters through `addAdHocFilters` (`datasource.ts:1127-1130`, `1073-1091`). The split path then calls `datasource.runQuery`, which calls `super.query`. `DataSourceWithBackend.query` runs `this.applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` on every target again (`packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185`). The request passed to `runQuery` still carries `filters` (`querySplitting.ts:315`, `337`), so the second pass adds the same filters a second time. I found no dedupe in `addLabelToQuery` (`modifyQuery.ts:147-214`).

Before this change the split path interpolated once, in the backend call. Now each ad hoc filter is appended twice, e.g. `{a="b", k="v", k="v"}` or a repeated `| k="v"`. Values that were already interpolated also get replaced a second time. The visible effect is a larger query in the inspector, in query history and in the Loki request. It could also change cache keys.

The interpolated step and expression are needed by `calculateStep` and `isLogsQuery`. A fix could pass the interpolated queries on in a form the second pass leaves unchanged, for example by dropping `filters` from the sub-request. I have not read how the backend treats `request.filters`, so that is untested. Alternatively, interpolate only the fields the splitter reads. No test covers `request.filters` on this path.

findings.title: Shard path interpolates three times: here, in each runSplitQuery sub-request, and in the backend query
findings.body:
`runShardSplitQuery` applies `applyTemplateVariables` once. Each shard group is then sent through `runSplitQuery` (`shardQuerySplitting.ts:163`), which applies it again (`querySplitting.ts:299`). `runQuery` then goes through `DataSourceWithBackend.query`, which applies it a third time (`DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185`). `subRequest` is built as `{ ...request, ... }` (`shardQuerySplitting.ts:154`), so `filters` and `scopedVars` are still on it. With ad hoc filters set, each one is added three times to the query sent to Loki, and every request in the shard loop does the same.

The interpolation done here is what `getSelectorForShardValues` needs to see the real stream selector, so it should stay. The repeat passes in `runSplitQuery` and the backend should be avoided, for example by not forwarding `filters` or by letting `runSplitQuery` skip interpolation when its caller has already done it. The `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` assertion in the shard test shows the redundancy.

findings.title: The test pins the number of interpolation calls at 5, which makes the redundancy look intended
findings.body: `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` is 1 call from `runShardSplitQuery` plus 4 calls from the per-group `runSplitQuery` runs. The assertion breaks if the shard grouping or group sizing changes, and it fixes the repeated interpolation in place. Assert on what is sent instead: the interpolated `expr` in the `runQuery` calls that follow. Add a case with `request.filters` that checks each ad hoc filter appears once in the sent expression. `applyTemplateVariables` is mocked in this file's `beforeEach` (line 56), so that case needs the real implementation, as the new test at line 84 uses.

contracts.action: runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables on each non-hidden target before partitioning
contracts.equivalent_path: DataSourceWithBackend.query applies applyTemplateVariables per target (DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185) when runQuery runs; runLiveQueryThroughBackend (datasource.ts:377) and the experimental streaming branch (datasource.ts:324) each interpolate once.
contracts.before_after: Before: split path left expr/step raw, so calculateStep, isLogsQuery and isQueryWithRangeVariable saw un-interpolated text, and interpolation happened once in the backend call. After: they see interpolated text, but runQuery then interpolates the same targets again with the same scopedVars and filters.
contracts.visible_effect: Step from a variable like $step now drives split sizing. Ad hoc filters appear duplicated in the request sent to Loki.
contracts.failure_mode: No new async call. A throw from applyTemplateVariables (e.g. addLabelToQuery with an empty filter key throws 'Need label to add to query.') now occurs synchronously in runSplitQuery, before any Observable is returned, instead of inside DataSourceWithBackend.query. This was not checked against how callers handle it.

contracts.action: runShardSplitQuery replaces interpolateVariablesInQueries(request.targets, request.scopedVars) with per-target applyTemplateVariables(…, request.filters)
contracts.equivalent_path: interpolateVariablesInQueries (datasource.ts:429-446) sets datasource ref, replaces expr and adds ad hoc filters from its adhocFilters argument. The old call omitted that argument, so no ad hoc filters were added here.
contracts.before_after: Before: one interpolation, without ad hoc filters, then the runSplitQuery and backend passes. After: expr, step and legendFormat are interpolated, ad hoc filters are added, __interval and __interval_ms are kept as passthrough, and the datasource ref is no longer set here. runSplitQuery and the backend then interpolate again.
contracts.visible_effect: Shard queries now get ad hoc filters and step/legendFormat interpolation. Filters are repeated across the three passes.
contracts.failure_mode: The shard-value lookup (getSelectorForShardValues, shardQuerySplitting.ts:252) now sees the selector with ad hoc filters added; the effect on the fetched shard list was not checked.

summary: The change interpolates targets in `runSplitQuery` and `runShardSplitQuery` so step and expression are resolved before splitting. `runQuery` then goes through `DataSourceWithBackend.query`, which applies `applyTemplateVariables` again with the same `filters`. Ad hoc filters therefore get appended twice on the plain split path and three times on the shard path, and I found no dedupe in `addLabelToQuery`. The new tests use a mock template service and no ad hoc filters, so they don't catch it. The shard test also pins the number of interpolation calls at 5.
